summary: This standards-track document describes the use of the Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm in the Internet Key Exchange Protocol version 2.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 8420 adds an IKEv2 hash-identifier value called Identity for signature algorithms such as Ed25519 and Ed448 that do not need a separate hashing step. A peer must signal support before EdDSA is used.

questions: how to use eddsa in ikev2
what is the identity hash in ikev2
what does the identity hash mean in ikev2
subtitle: How IKEv2 signals support for EdDSA signatures that do not need a separate hash.

tldr.problem: IKEv2's signature negotiation assumes signature algorithms use a separate hashing phase, while EdDSA accepts messages directly without prehashing.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the Identity hash identifier with value 5 to signal support for a signature algorithm such as Ed25519 or Ed448 that accepts arbitrary-size messages.
tldr.outcome: IKEv2 implementations use EdDSA only when the peer indicates Identity support, and must not use the prehashed EdDSA variants.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 8420's status as Proposed Standard. The RFC defines how EdDSA is signaled for use in IKEv2.

sections.title: EdDSA Does Not Need a Separate Hash
sections.content:
IKEv2 can negotiate signature algorithms through the SIGNATURE_HASH_ALGORITHMS notification, which lists supported hash algorithms. That mechanism assumes a signature algorithm first hashes a message and then signs the hash.

EdDSA methods Ed25519 and Ed448 accept messages of arbitrary size without prehashing. This RFC defines a notification value to indicate that a peer supports a signature algorithm with that property.
sections.plainLanguage: EdDSA can sign the message directly instead of hashing it first. IKEv2 needs a signal so peers know that no separate hash is used.

sections.title: The Identity Hash Identifier
sections.content:
The RFC assigns the name Identity and value 5 in the IKEv2 Hash Algorithms registry. Its presence in SIGNATURE_HASH_ALGORITHMS indicates support for at least one signature algorithm that accepts messages of arbitrary size, such as Ed25519 or Ed448.

Ed25519 and Ed448 are defined only with Identity and must not be sent to a receiver that has not indicated support. Ed25519ph and Ed448ph, the prehashed versions, must not be used in IKE.
sections.plainLanguage: A peer advertises Identity to show it supports a signature that does not need prehashing. Ed25519 and Ed448 can be used only after that support is signaled.

sections.title: Using Identity Only When Needed
sections.content:
The Identity value is intended only for supported and configured signature algorithms that accept arbitrary-size input. Implementations must include it in the notification when EdDSA is supported and configured.

The RFC says implementations should not include other hash algorithms in the notification if all supported and configured signature algorithms have this property.
sections.plainLanguage: Identity tells a peer that a configured signature method takes the full message without prehashing. Implementations should advertise it only when that kind of signature is available.
